title: Foreboding
text:
Foreboding


Foreboding is that long shadow

that little by little advances over

        the grass

when the sun abandons its empires...


Foreboding is the faint whisper

that runs through the fearful grass

        to tell it that night is coming.
editorial_note: The catalog title differs, but the visible body is 'Foreboding'; the source credits Carlos López Narváez's Spanish version.

title: Do Not Come Too Near a House of Rose...
text:
Do not come too near

a house of rose, for the ravages of a breeze

or the dew flooding it-one drop-

will bring down its frightened wall.


And do not try to bind the butterfly,

nor scale the hedges of rapture.

To find rest in the insecure

belongs to joy's very being.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the fragile rose-house and the final insight that joy rests in insecurity.

title: Pride
text:
We know our full height only

if someone says to our being: Rise!

And then, faithful to itself, it grows gigantic

until its stature reaches heaven.


Heroism in the human ring

would be the law of ordinary life

if we did not bow beneath the fear

of seeing and feeling ourselves like a king.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the poem's claim that human height appears only when summoned past fear.

title: When I Count the Seeds...
text:
When I count the seeds

sown down there

to flower so, side by side;


when I examine the people

who lie so low

to rise so high;


when I think that the garden

mortals will not see

has chance reap its buds

and draw lots for this bee,

I can do without summer, without complaint.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the seed/grave/garden logic of Dickinson as mediated through the Spanish text.

title: The Ring
text:
On my finger I had a ring.

The breeze wandered among the trees.

The day was blue, warm, and beautiful.

And I fell asleep on the fine grass.


When I woke, startled, I looked at

my pure hand in the clear afternoon.

The ring was no longer on my finger.

All I possess now in this world

is a memory of golden color.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the lost ring as a small vanished possession reduced to golden memory.
